ratings_why.fun: Three builds that read differently (flood high, swing, drain dry) and the swing engine is a real puzzle; some cards are plain 'on change, +stats' bookkeeping.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7 because your own visible water Level hurts both front rows, so you build your front row around weather you set yourself; no current tribe or typical auto-battler tribe makes a symmetric board hazard its core.

verdict_why: One real clarity fix (Tail-Slapper at Level 0); otherwise it reads well and further passes would mostly make it different.

points.text: Tail-Slapper says 'Flood again', but the Flood rule only floods above Level 0 and floors damage at 1, so a player can't tell if it does 1 to every front unit at Level 0 or nothing. Say 'If your Level is above 0'.
The tenths are the one thing a player can't do at a glance; show each front-row unit's coming Flood loss (and a dry/afloat mark) on the board while recruiting.
Hendrika's steps after an Aaltje 'for this fight' Raise lasting only for the fight lives in the rationale; put it in the Raise/Drain keyword text so it reads on the board.
Inspecting Heemraad only works from the back row; 'the front-row units in front of this' would tell a player where to put it.
Objecting Coot's sell-to-Raise is a thin link to coots objecting to boundaries; a coot that Raises when you move a unit to a new slot would carry the territory squabble in play.

standouts.why: Kobus minuting everything twice is the lore done as a rule, and it reads in one line.
Winter Raft's frozen canals at Level 0 is a lovely, readable reason for coots in the drain build.
The Spaarndam Pup plugging the dike as 'your Floods can't harm you' is fantasy and payoff in one sentence.

weakest.why: Sell-to-Raise works but the woodland story behind it doesn't show in what it does.
Old Bram is a generic 'on change, buff the smallest' body; the engineer waking at a trickle is only in the name.
The diagonal 'in front of' placement is easy to misread, and the card is a plain buffer otherwise.

flags.note: What 'Flood again' does at Level 0 isn't said.
Hendrika with Kobus and Master of the Nine Mills gives every unit about +10/+10 a turn; bounded but worth the owner's eye.
Golden Pup at Level 5 floods twice into both enemy rows while yours stay dry; could decide fights before any attack.
